'The only one who is not at peace is you. And that peace is yours to claim — whenever you are ready.'
dialogue.home:
'You will return when the wind is ready. And the wind is always ready — it is you who are not.'

He smiles at your expression.

'You have not yet finished your voyage. But you will. And when you do, you will find that home was never a place — it was a feeling. And that feeling has been with you all along.'
dialogue.sea:
'The sea is God's breath upon the water,' he says softly. 'It is older than the mountains, older than sin, older than memory. It carries prayers in its currents and secrets in its depths.

'You have sailed upon it for three years, Mael Duin. You have learned its language — the rhythm of the tides, the warnings in the clouds, the songs in the creaking of your curragh's timbers.

'The sea has changed you. It has washed away what was not essential. Look at your hands. They are the same hands that pushed off from the Aran shore. But the man they belong to is not the same.

'That is what the sea does. It is a mirror, and it shows you who you truly are.'
dialogue.death:
'Death is not the enemy, Mael Duin. It is the doorway. Your father walked through it before you. You will walk through it after. The only question is what you carry in your hands when you do.

'Will you carry a sword? Or will you carry peace?'

ailill.name: Ailill Ochair Ága
ailill.description: A giant of a man with a beard like rusted iron and arms thick as mast timbers. He is laughing — always laughing — with a drinking horn in his fist. His sword, Wolf's Fang, leans against his throne. He is the Wolf of the Arans, and he does not know this is his last night alive.

dialogue.greeting:
Ailill looks up and grins. His teeth are white against his beard.

"Well, well! A visitor! Come, sit, drink! The night is young and so are we — well, I'm not young, but I'm still here, and that's what counts!

You have the look of a storyteller. Or a spy. Or a storyteller who is also a spy. Either way, you're welcome at my table. Pull up a bench!

The mead is sweet and the company is finer. What brings you to my hall?"
dialogue.dead:
Ailill lies still on the cold sand. His eyes are open, staring at the grey sky. The tide washes over his feet, and his sword — Wolf's Fang — is still clasped in his dead hand.

He does not answer. He cannot. The Wolf of the Arans is gone.
dialogue.death:
Ailill lies still on the cold sand. His eyes are open, staring at the grey sky. The tide washes over his feet, and his sword — Wolf's Fang — is still clasped in his dead hand.

He does not answer. He cannot. The Wolf of the Arans is gone.
dialogue.father:
"My son? Mael Duin? He's asleep by the fire. Barely a year old and already he has the grip of a warrior. He grabbed my finger today and would not let go. I told his mother: this one will be a fighter.

I hope he grows up strong. I hope he grows up kind. I hope he grows up to be a better man than his father. That's all any father can wish for."
dialogue.war:
"War? War is a young man's game, and I am no longer young. But I am still good at it. The Northern Isles sent a raiding party last month. I sent them back in pieces. They will think twice before crossing the Wolf again.

But tonight? Tonight we feast. War can wait until morning."
dialogue.wife:
"My wife? She is the best of me. She keeps me grounded, keeps me human. Without her, I would be just another brute with a sword. With her, I am... something more.

She worries. That is her job. My job is to make sure she has nothing to worry about."

mother.name: Your Mother
mother.description: A woman with tired eyes and a gentle face. She sits by the cradle, her hand resting on it as if she is afraid to let go. She has not laughed all night. She knows something is wrong.

dialogue.greeting:
She looks up at you with eyes that have seen too much.

"Shh. The baby is sleeping. He is so small, so fragile. I look at him and I see his father — the same stubborn chin, the same way of furrowing his brow.

I hope he grows up to be a better man than Ailill. I hope he grows up at all.

The world is cruel and the sea is crueler. But perhaps... perhaps there is hope for him yet."
dialogue.ailill:
"He does not know when to stop. The feasting, the fighting, the laughing. He lives every day as if it is his last. And one day, it will be.

I have told him a hundred times: the Northern raiders will come back. They always do. But he just laughs and says, "Let them come. I will be waiting."

I fear he will wait for them once too often."
dialogue.baby:
"Mael Duin. My son. He has his father's strength but — I pray — none of his recklessness. I look at him and I see a future I will not live to witness. But that is the way of things. Mothers give birth to children who will bury them. That is the natural order.

I just hope he remembers me. When I am gone. I hope he knows I loved him."

ailill_keep.name: Ailill's Keep — The Night of the Wolf
ailill_keep.description: The great hall of Ailill Ochair Ága, the Wolf of the Arans. Torchlight. Feasting. The last night of peace.
ailill_keep.detailed_desc:
The great hall of Ailill Ochair Ága blazes with torchlight. Warriors line the benches, their faces red with firelight and mead. A whole pig roasts on a spit the size of a small tree. The air smells of woodsmoke, roasted meat, and the salt of the sea.

At the head of the hall sits AILILL himself — a giant of a man with a beard like rusted iron and arms thick as mast timbers. He is laughing, his head thrown back, a drinking horn in his fist. His sword — the famous 'Wolf's Fang' — leans against his throne.

"Tonight we feast!" he roars, and the hall cheers. "Tomorrow we plan the next raid! But tonight — tonight we drink to the sea that gives us life, the earth that feeds us, and the enemies who make victory so sweet!"

In a cradle near the fire, an INFANT sleeps — his newborn son, Mael Duin. Ailill's wife watches over him, her hand resting on the cradle. She does not laugh. She has not laughed all night.

A DRUID sits in the shadows, his eyes on the flames. He has not touched his food.

Outside, the wind howls. But it is not the wind. It is the sound of oars in the night.

ailill_beach.name: The Strand — Where the Wolf Fell
ailill_beach.description: A grey beach under a grey sky. The tide is coming in, washing over the body of a warrior.
ailill_beach.detailed_desc:
You step out of the hall and into a world that has changed.

The raiders came in the night — men from the Northern Isles, their boats painted with the skulls of their enemies. They came not for plunder, but for blood. A blood feud, older than anyone remembers, older than the stones of this island.

Ailill fought them on the beach, his back to the sea, Wolf's Fang singing in his hands. He took seven of them with him before they brought him down. The last raider — a grey-bearded man with one eye — drove a spear through his heart.

Now Ailill lies on the strand, the tide washing his feet. His sword is still in his hand. His eyes are open, staring at the grey sky. He looks almost peaceful.

A WOMAN kneels beside him — his wife, your mother. She does not weep. She is past weeping. She holds a lock of his hair in her hand.

A DRUID stands nearby, holding the infant Mael Duin. The baby is crying. He doesn't know why.

The druid looks at you — through you — and speaks to the ghost you are:

"You will grow up not knowing this moment. But it will live in your blood. It will call you to the sea one day. And when it does, you will not return the same man who left."

(Type EAST to return to the hall, or type ONWARD to move forward in time.)

foster_village.name: The Foster Village — Ten Years Later
foster_village.description: A small village on the Aran Islands. Children play in the dirt. Goats wander freely. Life continues.
foster_village.detailed_desc:
Ten years have passed. The world has moved on.

You stand at the edge of a small village — not the great keep of your father, but a humble cluster of stone huts. Goats wander the lanes. A dog sleeps in the sun. Children chase each other with sticks, pretending to be warriors.

One of them is YOU — Mael Duin, aged ten. You are small for your age, but quick. You have your father's eyes and your mother's silence. You do not know about Ailill. You have been told your father was a fisherman who drowned.

Your FOSTER MOTHER — the woman who found Ailill's body — watches from the door of her hut. She is kind, but her eyes hold a secret. She looks at you sometimes and her face twists with something you don't understand. Grief. Guilt. Love.

An old DRUID visits the village often. He brings herbs and wisdom. He always stops to talk to you.

"You have the look of a man who will cross the sea," he tells you. "You just don't know it yet."

(Type ONWARD to grow older. Type TALK TO to speak with people.)

training_field.name: The Training Field — Five Years Later
training_field.description: A grassy field by the sea. Wooden swords lie scattered on the ground. Young men train here.
training_field.detailed_desc:
Five more years have passed. Fifteen summers. Fifteen winters. You are no longer a child.

The training field overlooks the sea. Here, the young men of the village learn to fight — not because they expect war, but because the sea is cruel and the world is crueler.

You have grown tall. Your shoulders have broadened. When you pick up a practice sword, it feels natural in your hand — as if it remembers something your mind does not.

You train with CONGANCHNES, a young warrior with a legendary gift: his skin cannot be cut. He is your best friend and your fiercest rival. He beats you every time, but you're getting closer.

"You're improving," he says, knocking your sword out of your hand. "You only lasted five seconds longer than last week. Soon you'll last almost a minute." He grins.

FERGUS, the navigator, sits on a rock, studying the stars even though it's daytime. "The stars say there's a storm coming," he mutters. "Also that I should have eaten less cheese."

DIURÁN, the poet's apprentice, sits under a tree, composing verses about the battle he's imagining you'll have one day.

Your foster mother watches from the edge of the field. She looks proud. And sad.

(Type ONWARD to the next chapter. Type TALK TO to speak with your companions.)

feast_hall.name: The Feast Hall — Twenty Years Old
feast_hall.description: The same hall where Ailill once feasted. Different faces. Different songs. But the same silence beneath the laughter.
feast_hall.detailed_desc:
Twenty years old. A man, by every measure that matters.

You stand in the great hall of the Aran Islands — the same hall where your father drank and laughed on the last night of his life. You don't know that. But something about this place has always felt strange to you. Familiar. Haunted.

The hall is full tonight. Warriors, farmers, their wives and children. A feast to celebrate the summer solstice. The mead flows freely. Stories are told. Songs are sung. You sit among your companions — Conganchnes, Fergus, Diurán — laughing at a joke that isn't very funny.

And then a man speaks.

He is a warrior from a neighboring territory — drunk, jealous, mean-spirited. His name is LORCÁN. He has been watching you all night.

"So," he says, loud enough for the hall to hear, "here sits Mael Duin, the great warrior. The man with no father. The bastard of Inishmore."

The hall goes silent.

Your friends tense. Conganchnes reaches for his sword. Diurán stops writing.

"You don't know, do you?" Lorcán grins. "They never told you. Your father wasn't a fisherman. Your father was Ailill Ochair Ága — the Wolf of the Arans. And he was murdered. Slain on the beach like a dog. While you slept in your cradle."

The world stops.

Your blood burns. Your hand finds your sword. The hall holds its breath.

druid_sanctuary.name: The Druid's Sanctuary
druid_sanctuary.description: A hidden grove where an old druid lives. The air smells of herbs and old secrets.
druid_sanctuary.detailed_desc:
You burst into the druid's grove like a storm. The old man is sitting by his fire, stirring a pot. He does not look surprised to see you.

"I was wondering when you'd come," he says.

"Is it true?" You can barely speak. Your hands are shaking. "Is Ailill Ochair Ága my father?"

The druid is silent for a long time. Then he nods.

"Yes. Ailill was your father. And he was murdered — by raiders from the Northern Isles, men who had a blood feud with his family stretching back three generations. They came in the night, burned his hall, and killed him on the beach."

"Why didn't you tell me?"

"Because I wanted you to live your own life," the druid says. "Not the life of a dead man's revenge. But I see now that the sea will call you, whether I wish it or not. The blood of the Wolf runs in your veins. And wolves do not stay in their dens when there is hunting to be done."

He reaches into his robe and pulls out a shimmering SILKEN THREAD.

"Take this. Tie it to your mast. It will guide you through the mists. And take exactly three times nine men — no more, no less. Twenty-seven souls. Not twenty-six. Not twenty-eight. Twenty-seven."

"Is there anything else?" you ask.

"Yes," the druid says. "When you find the men who killed your father... you may find that killing them is not what you truly want."

He presses the thread into your hand. It glows faintly, warm as a living thing.

(The Magic Thread has been added to your inventory.)

village_harbor.name: The Harbor — The Day of Departure
village_harbor.description: A grey morning. A curragh on the beach. Twenty-seven men. The start of the voyage.
village_harbor.detailed_desc:
Three days later, you stand on the beach where your father died. The tide is low, and the sand is wet and hard beneath your feet.

Before you, a CURRAGH — a boat of wicker and hide, built for the open sea. It is larger than any curragh you've ever seen, built by the village's best shipwrights in a fever of preparation. It will carry twenty-seven men. Not one more. Not one less.

Your CREW assembles on the sand:

DIURÁN, the poet, carrying more parchment than provisions. "I will make this voyage into an epic that will be sung for a thousand years," he announces. "Assuming we survive it."

CONGANCHNES, the invulnerable, sharpening his sword with slow, deliberate strokes. "I've been waiting for a real fight," he says. "The practice field is getting boring."

FERGUS, the navigator, staring at the sky. "The stars say we'll have fair winds. They also say I should have brought a warmer cloak."

Twenty-four other men — farmers, fishermen, warriors — each with their own reasons for following you across the edge of the world.

Your FOSTER MOTHER stands apart from the crowd. She does not weep. She has done enough weeping for one lifetime. She holds out a small leather pouch — your father's signet ring, kept hidden all these years.

"He would be proud of you," she says. "Now go. And come back alive."

The druid raises his hand in blessing. The sun breaks through the clouds.

The tide is turning. The sea is waiting.

(Type WEST to set sail. Type TALK TO to speak with your crew.)

fathers_tomb.name: Ailill's Cairn
fathers_tomb.description: A pile of stones on a windswept hill, overlooking the sea. A warrior's grave.
fathers_tomb.detailed_desc:
Before you leave, you climb the hill alone.

A cairn of grey stones marks the place where Ailill Ochair Ága was laid to rest. No inscription. No marker. Just stones. The sea wind whistles through the gaps.

You place your hand on the cairn. The stones are cold. The wind is cold. But somewhere beneath the chill, you feel warmth — the last ember of a fire that burned brighter than most.

"I will find them," you say. "And I will do what must be done."

The wind answers with silence. The sea answers with waves. The stones answer with stillness.

You turn and walk back to the harbor.

home.name: Your Village — The Aran Islands
home.description: Your village on the Aran Islands. The stone huts huddle against the wind, and the grey Atlantic stretches to the horizon.
home.detailed_desc:
You stand at the edge of your village on Inishmore, the largest of the Aran Islands. The stone walls of your people's huts are worn smooth by centuries of Atlantic wind. Salt-spray hangs in the air. Somewhere, a dog barks. A child laughs.

To the west, the endless grey ocean stretches toward the edge of the known world. To the east, the fields of Ireland are a distant green smudge.

Your CURRAGH — a sturdy boat of wicker and hide — is pulled up on the beach, ready to sail. It smells of fish, salt, and adventure.

The memory of your father's murder burns in your chest like a hot coal. Your hand drifts to your sword-hilt before you catch yourself.

An old DRUID sits by a fire near the village center. He is stirring a pot that smells like boiled nettles and regret.

sea1.name: The Open Sea
sea1.description: Your curragh rises and falls on the grey Atlantic. The coast of Ireland is a fading line behind you.
sea1.detailed_desc:
The wind fills your square-rigged sail. Your crew of 27 men man the oars, their faces set with determination — and a hint of seasickness.

The druid's Magic Thread flutters from the mast, pulling gently to the west as if guided by an invisible hand.

Ahead, the sea stretches endlessly. Diurán the poet is already writing about the experience. Conganchnes the invulnerable stands at the prow, scanning for enemies. Fergus mutters to himself, counting stars he can't yet see.

Islands dot the horizon in every direction. Each one promises strangeness.

island_ants.name: Island of the Giant Ants
island_ants.description: An island covered in trees bearing golden fruit. The ground trembles with the marching of giant ants.
island_ants.detailed_desc:
You step onto a beach of white sand. Beyond it, a forest of strange trees rises — each one laden with golden, glowing fruit that never rots.

But the trees are crawling with ANTS. Each ant is the size of a horse, with mandibles that could snap an oar in two.

They seem to be... farming the trees. They tend the fruit with surprising care, almost like gardeners. One ant is gently polishing a golden fruit with its forelegs.

One of them is watching you. It tilts its head. It seems more curious than hostile.

A path leads INto the grove where the queen ant holds court.

blocked.in: giant ants block the path — they seem to fear the speaking birds

ants_grove.name: The Ant Grove
ants_grove.description: The heart of the ant colony. A massive queen ant sits atop a mound of golden fruit.
ants_grove.detailed_desc:
The grove opens into a clearing where the QUEEN ANT — the size of a house — sits regally upon a throne of woven branches and golden fruit.

She regards you with compound eyes that reflect the world in a thousand fragments. Each fragment shows you from a different angle. You have never felt so thoroughly seen.

The fruit here is piled high. A single branch hangs low, offering its golden bounty.

The worker ants have stopped their labor. They watch you in complete silence. Even the wind holds its breath.

island_birds.name: Island of the Speaking Birds
island_birds.description: An island of sheer cliffs covered in birds of every color. They sing in human tongues.
island_birds.detailed_desc:
The cliffs rise like cathedral walls, every ledge occupied by a bird. They are not ordinary birds — they speak. Not just mimicry, but actual conversation.

"Welcome, hairless ones!" cries a red-feathered creature.
"Did you bring snacks?" asks another, hopping closer hopefully.
"I saw a fish once that looked just like you!" adds a third.

At the top of the cliff, an ENORMOUS OLD BIRD perches — ancient, half-blind, and clearly the elder of this feathered parliament. It hasn't spoken yet.

A single, iridescent feather lies at the base of the cliff, humming faintly.

birds_nest.name: The Ancient Bird's Perch
birds_nest.description: The nest of the Ancient Bird, built from silver twigs and lined with gold.
birds_nest.detailed_desc:
The Ancient Bird fixes you with one milky eye.

"Mael Duin," it says. Its voice is like old parchment being folded. "I have been expecting you. Well, not you specifically. I've been expecting someone. It's been a long time since anyone climbed up here. My legs don't work like they used to."

It shifts on its nest, revealing a stash of shiny objects — coins, buttons, a thimble, a bronze brooch, and what looks like a dragon's tooth.

"Take what you need," it says. "I'm too old to guard treasure. I mostly just nap and complain about the weather."

island_cat.name: Island of the Cat
island_cat.description: A small, tidy island with a single stone house. A massive black cat sits by the door.
island_cat.detailed_desc:
This island is immaculate. The grass is perfectly trimmed, the path is swept clean, and a stone house stands at the center with a neatly painted door. A welcome mat reads "WIPE YOUR PAWS."

Before the door, on a golden throne, sits a CAT.

It is the largest cat you have ever seen — the size of a bear. Its fur is black as ink, and its eyes are ancient green gold. It wears a small golden crown that looks surprisingly natural on its head.

It licks a paw with careful dignity, then looks at you. It does not blink. Cats don't need to blink. They need you to know they don't need to blink.

You get the distinct feeling you are being judged and found wanting.

island_laughing.name: Island of the Laughing People
island_laughing.description: An island where EVERYONE is laughing. Babies laugh. Dogs laugh. Even the trees seem to chuckle.
island_laughing.detailed_desc:
As you step ashore, a wave of laughter hits you. Everyone — and everything — on this island is laughing.

A farmer laughs as he plows. His horse laughs. The chickens laugh so hard they fall off their perches. A woman offers you a cup of water, laughing so hard she spills half of it.

In the center of the village, a KING sits on a one-legged stool, laughing uproariously at absolutely nothing visible. He laughs until he cries, then laughs at his own tears.

Your crew is starting to giggle. Conganchnes looks deeply uncomfortable. He has not laughed since 1142 and he is not about to start now.

glass_bridge.name: Island of the Glass Bridge
glass_bridge.description: A glittering island with a bridge made entirely of crystal, leading to a palace beyond.
glass_bridge.detailed_desc:
A palace of white marble gleams in the distance. But to reach it, you must cross a BRIDGE made entirely of transparent glass, suspended over a chasm of swirling mist.

The glass is perfectly clear. You can see straight through it to the jagged rocks below. The bridge is about a hundred feet long and looks like it was made by someone who had never heard the phrase 'safety first.'

A beautiful woman stands on the far side of the bridge, beckoning.

"Cross, brave sailor. I will not let you fall."

You notice two things that might help: a SHARD OF GLASS lies at the base of the bridge, broken off from the edge. And in your heart, you feel the HERMIT'S BLESSING could carry you across on faith alone.

Without either, the bridge is certain death.

blocked.cross: the bridge is made of transparent glass over a bottomless chasm — you need the Glass Shard to test its strength or the Hermit's Blessing to cross on faith

glass_palace.name: The Glass Palace
glass_palace.description: A palace of crystal and light. Music plays from nowhere, and the air smells of honey.
glass_palace.detailed_desc:
You step into a palace that seems built from frozen light. Every surface reflects a thousand colors in a thousand different ways. Music — harps and flutes — plays without any musician.

A beautiful woman offers you a seat on cushions of silk. "Stay," she whispers. "Rest. You have traveled so far."

This place feels like a dream. It also feels like a trap. The floor is suspiciously transparent in places — you can see the chasm below. The palace isn't built on the ground; it's suspended over the void.

The woman's smile never reaches her eyes.

A voice in your head whispers: 'Stay and you will forget your quest. Leave and you will remember.'

Type YES to stay (lose time, risk losing a crew member).
Type NO to leave the palace behind.

island_smithy.name: Island of the Smithy
island_smithy.description: An island of volcanic rock, dominated by a massive forge that belches fire and smoke.
island_smithy.detailed_desc:
The air shimmers with heat. A mountain of slag and cinder rises from the center of the island, topped by a FORGE the size of a hill.

CLANG. CLANG. CLANG.

Each hammer strike shakes the ground beneath your feet. The vibrations travel up through your legs and rattle your teeth.

A GIANT works the bellows — each breath of the bellows sends a gale across the island. You realize the bellows are what create storms at sea. The giant sneezes, and a bolt of lightning cracks across the sky, followed by a thunderclap that rocks the boat.

"...Bless you," says a crew member quietly.

The giant hasn't noticed you yet. He's too busy hammering a block of metal that's glowing like a small sun.

island_women.name: Island of Women
island_women.description: An island of perpetual sunset, where beautiful women feast, dance, and sing endlessly.
island_women.detailed_desc:
You step onto an island that seems untouched by time. The sun is always just setting, painting everything in gold and rose. The air is warm and smells of honey and jasmine.

Beautiful women in silken gowns approach, offering trays of roasted meats, fresh bread, and honeyed wine. Music — a harp and a flute — floats on the warm air.

Your crew is already drooling. Diurán is composing poetry. Conganchnes is blushing. Fergus has forgotten how to navigate.

At the center of the feast, a QUEEN sits on a throne of flowers. She smiles at you — a smile that promises everything and costs nothing.

sea_monsters.name: The Sea of Monsters
sea_monsters.description: Still, glassy water that feels wrong. Something moves beneath the surface.
sea_monsters.detailed_desc:
The sea is unnaturally calm — flat as glass. Not a breath of wind stirs. The water is dark green, almost black, and impossibly deep.

Your crew rows nervously. Too quietly. Too watchfully. Oars dip into the water without a splash, as if the sea itself is holding its breath.

Something HUGE passes beneath the boat. A shadow the size of your curragh glides in the depths. It circles once. Twice.

Then — a giant hand erupts from the water, grabbing the side of your boat! Webbed fingers the size of hammers grip the gunwale. The boat lurches violently.

sea2.name: The Deeper Sea
sea2.description: The water has changed color — a deep, midnight blue. Strange lights flicker beneath the surface.
sea2.detailed_desc:
You have sailed beyond the familiar waters into the deeper sea. The coastline of Ireland is long gone. The sky is a different shade of grey here — somehow older, more ancient, as if this sky was hung before humans learned to name things.

The druid's Magic Thread pulls steadily westward. The wind has a different voice — it whispers names you don't recognize in a language that sounds almost like Irish but isn't.

Fergus squints at the horizon. 'We're in uncharted waters now, Captain. The stars are different here. They have... stranger names. Also, I think that cloud just waved at me.'

Bioluminescent creatures drift past the boat, trailing sparks of cold fire. The water glows where your oars dip in, leaving trails of light.

island_culdees.name: Island of the Culdees
island_culdees.description: A peaceful island with a small monastery. A bell rings itself, calling the monks to prayer.
island_culdees.detailed_desc:
A monastery of grey stone stands on this quiet island. The Culdees — anchorites devoted to God — tend a garden of herbs and vegetables with patient, weathered hands.

A SILVER BELL hangs in a small tower. It rings of its own accord, at the exact hour of prayer. No one rings it. It simply decides it's time, and rings.

The monks pay you no mind. They are busy praying, gardening, and ignoring the mortal world with a dedication that is almost impressive.

One monk looks up from his weeding and nods once. 'The bell knows when it's needed,' he says. 'Do you?' He goes back to weeding before you can answer.

The silver bell is within reach. It would certainly fetch a price. But stealing from monks feels... wrong.

prophecy_tower.name: Island of Prophecy
prophecy_tower.description: An island with a single tower of crystal, rising from the sea like a prism.
prophecy_tower.detailed_desc:
A tower of pure crystal rises from the sea, catching the light and scattering it into rainbows. The sight is so beautiful it makes Diurán weep. 'I'll never be able to describe this adequately,' he sobs, writing furiously.

A door of silver stands open. Inside, stairs spiral upward. The steps are made of glass, and beneath them, you can see the sea. It's a long way down.

At the top of the tower, a YOUNG BOY sits cross-legged on nothing — he's floating a few inches above the floor. He's reading a book that has no pages, yet he turns each invisible leaf with great concentration.

He looks up and grins. 'Took you long enough! I've been waiting since page three.'

hermit_rock.name: The Hermit's Rock
hermit_rock.description: A bare rock in the middle of the ocean. A holy man stands upon it, one with the elements.
hermit_rock.detailed_desc:
You approach a solitary ROCK jutting from the sea. It is no larger than your curragh. The waves crash against it with furious regularity, yet the man standing on top does not so much as sway.

Upon it stands a HERMIT, soaked by spray, lashed by wind, his eyes closed in prayer. His beard moves in the breeze like a living thing. His robes are patched in a dozen colors.

At his feet, an OTTER sits, holding a fish in its mouth. The otter looks at you with an expression that clearly says 'This is my fish. Get your own.'

The hermit opens his eyes and looks directly at you. His gaze is unsettling — it feels like he's looking through you, not at you.

"I was wondering when you'd get here," he says. "The otter caught a large one today — there's enough for everyone. Sit. Eat. Tell me why you're really here."

island_four_fences.name: Island of the Four Fences
island_four_fences.description: An island divided by four fences — gold, silver, copper, and crystal. You must choose the right one.
island_four_fences.detailed_desc:
A flat, grey island stretches before you. It is divided into four sections by four different fences.

The first fence is made of GOLD — gleaming, magnificent, clearly the most valuable. A gate stands open. A path beyond it leads invitingly toward a treasure chest.

The second fence is made of SILVER — elegant, understated, with a latch that lifts easily. Beyond it, the path is slightly overgrown but still clear.

The third fence is made of COPPER — humble, practical, with a simple rope holding the gate shut. Beyond it, the path is barely visible, winding through wild grass.

The fourth fence is made of CRYSTAL — delicate, beautiful, but it looks like it would shatter at a touch. Beyond it, a magnificent palace gleams on the horizon.

A faded sign reads: 'Beyond one fence lies a great treasure. Beyond the others, only regret. Choose wisely.'

The answer seems obvious. But maybe that's the trap.

island_salmon.name: Island of the Wisdom Salmon
island_salmon.description: An island with a single stream running through it, filled with silver salmon that leap against the current.
island_salmon.detailed_desc:
A small, green island with a crystal-clear stream running from a spring in the center to the sea.

The stream is FULL of salmon — fat, silver, magnificent fish that leap against the current with incredible determination. They move like thoughts — quick, purposeful, elusive.

But these are no ordinary salmon. When you look into their eyes, you see... understanding. They look back at you with the patient wisdom of creatures who have seen civilizations rise and fall.

A small sign on the bank reads: 'He who eats of the Salmon of Wisdom gains the knowledge of all things. But catching one requires cunning, for they are wiser than any fish has a right to be.'

The salmon look at you smugly. They know you don't have a fishing rod. One of them flicks its tail and says — actually says, in a clear voice — 'Nice try, land-walker.'

four_fences_gold.name: The Golden Gate — Greed's Reward
four_fences_gold.description: You chose the gold gate. It was a trap.
four_fences_gold.detailed_desc:
The moment you step through the golden gate, it SLAMS shut behind you. The golden bars grow thorns. The path ahead dissolves into mist.

From the mist, a voice: 'You chose what glitters. Now you must pay.'

A golden spike shoots from the ground. You barely dodge it. Your crew scrambles to escape. In the chaos, one of your items falls into a crevice and is lost forever.

You barely make it back to the gate, which has reopened. Your crew is shaken. One item is gone. The lesson: greed has a price.

four_fences_silver.name: The Silver Gate — Elegance Unrewarded
four_fences_silver.description: You chose the silver gate. A dead end.
four_fences_silver.detailed_desc:
The silver gate opens onto a path that winds through beautiful gardens. Flowers bloom in impossible colors. Fountains sing. It is lovely.

It is also a circle. The path leads nowhere — it brings you back to the starting point.

You have wasted time. The silver gate was beautiful but empty. The real treasure lies elsewhere.

four_fences_copper.name: The Copper Gate — Humility Rewarded
four_fences_copper.description: You chose the copper gate. The humble path. You chose wisely.
four_fences_copper.detailed_desc:
The copper gate swings open with a sound like a contented sigh. The path beyond is simple — packed earth, wildflowers, the smell of rain.

At the end of the path sits a small stone pedestal. On it rests a BRONZE KEY that turns in place of its own accord, as if it cannot stop moving.

A voice on the wind: 'You chose humility over pride. The key to the turning world is yours.'

The key is meant for the Revolving Castle. With it, you can choose the right door.

four_fences_crystal.name: The Crystal Gate — Fragile Beauty
four_fences_crystal.description: You chose the crystal gate. It shattered.
four_fences_crystal.detailed_desc:
The crystal gate is beautiful — delicate, rainbow-shot, perfect.

It is also as fragile as it looks. The moment you touch it, the entire gate shatters into a million pieces. Shards fly everywhere.

One of your crew members is cut badly. They will need time to recover. You cannot take them further into danger.

You lose a crew member. The crystal gate had no answer — only pain.

sea3.name: The Final Sea
sea3.description: The water is black as ink. The sky swirls with colors you've never seen. The end is near.
sea3.detailed_desc:
This is the edge of the known world. The sea here is dark and still — no fish, no birds, no wind. Just your breath and the creak of the curragh.

The Magic Thread glows brightly, pulling with purpose. You feel that your journey is almost at an end. The air tastes different here — older, like a room that's been sealed for centuries.

Diurán has stopped writing. He stares at the horizon, pale. 'Captain... I think we're close. I can feel it in my bones. Also, my quill just wrote 'DEATH' on its own. Probably a coincidence.'

Islands dot the darkness like scattered jewels. One of them must be the home of your father's killers. Or it might be another wonder. At this point, you're not sure which is which.

serpent_island.name: Island of the Great Snake
serpent_island.description: An island circled by a serpent so large it forms a continuous ring around the land.
serpent_island.detailed_desc:
You approach an island that is encircled by an enormous SNAKE — its body forms a complete ring around the land, head to tail. The scales are the size of shields, each one a different shade of purple and green.

As you draw near, the serpent raises its head — large enough to swallow your boat whole — and hisses. The sound is like a thousand swords being drawn at once.

But it doesn't attack. It just... watches. Its scales shimmer with a purple iridescence. It blinks slowly. One eye is the size of your curragh.

There is a narrow gap between the serpent's head and tail. You could slip through if you're quick.

Purple herbs grow on the island — the antidote to the serpent's poison. The serpent seems to be... guarding them? Or growing them?

blocked.through: the serpent blocks your way — it responds to the sound of silver

serpent_island_center.name: Within the Serpent's Ring
serpent_island_center.description: The center of the serpent-ringed island. Peaceful, fertile, eerily quiet.
serpent_island_center.detailed_desc:
The center of the island is surprisingly idyllic — green grass, a small spring, and the purple antidote herbs growing in abundance. It's like a hidden garden, protected from the rest of the world.

A stone altar stands at the center, carved with ouroboros — the snake eating its own tail. The carving is so old that the edges have worn smooth.

The serpent's head looms above you, but it makes no move to attack. It seems to be... waiting. Maybe it wants you to understand something.

A quiet voice — perhaps your own thought, perhaps the island's — whispers: 'The serpent guards not the island, but the wisdom within.'

black_pig.name: Island of the Black Pig
black_pig.description: An island with a single massive apple tree made of gold. A black pig guards it.
black_pig.detailed_desc:
A single tree stands on this island — an apple tree whose trunk, branches, and leaves are made of solid GOLD. Golden apples hang from its branches, glowing with an inner light.

At the base of the tree, a BLACK PIG the size of a cow snoozes contentedly. Its sides heave with each breath. Drool — liquid gold — pools beneath its snout.

The pig's tusks are the size of daggers. Its snout twitches as it dreams of... probably truffles. Or world domination. Hard to tell.

A sign next to the tree reads: "Take one apple, lose one hand."

The handwriting is surprisingly good for a pig. There's a small footnote that says 'No, seriously. I will bite you.'

speaking_skull.name: Island of the Thorny Bush
speaking_skull.description: An island with a single thorny bush growing through an old human skull. The skull speaks.
speaking_skull.detailed_desc:
On this small, barren island, a single thorny bush grows from a crack in the rock. There is nothing else. No trees, no grass, no sign of life except the bush.

A HUMAN SKULL is impaled on one of its thorns. The bone is yellowed with age, polished smooth by centuries of wind and rain.

As you approach, the skull's jaw drops open, and a voice rasps from its empty mouth:

"A visitor! Do you have any idea how long I've been sitting here? Decades! Centuries! And let me tell you, the view doesn't improve. Just bushes. Bushes and more bushes."

The skull's empty eye sockets seem to fix you with an expectant stare. Despite having no facial muscles, it manages to convey profound boredom.

island_water_horse.name: Island of the Water Horse
island_water_horse.description: A small, grassy island where a magnificent white horse stands on the water's surface as if it were solid ground.
island_water_horse.detailed_desc:
The island is little more than a grassy knoll emerging from the dark sea. But standing on the WATER beside it — not in it, ON it — is a magnificent WHITE HORSE.

Its mane flows like seaweed. Its hooves rest on the surface of the sea as if on marble. It looks at you with eyes that are deep, dark pools — bottomless, hypnotic.

"Welcome, traveler," it says. Its voice is smooth as silk and twice as slippery. "I can carry you across the ocean faster than any ship. I can take you anywhere you wish to go. Just climb on my back."

Your crew shifts uneasily. Fergus whispers: 'Captain, I don't think that's a horse. I think that's a kelpie. If you ride it, it'll drag you to the bottom of the sea and eat your liver.'

The horse smiles. It has too many teeth. Far too many.

blocked.ride: the kelpie's eyes are hypnotic — you need something to break its spell

water_horse_doom.name: The Kelpie's Domain
water_horse_doom.description: A shimmering underwater realm where the kelpie's true form flickers between horse and shadow.
water_horse_doom.detailed_desc:
You pull out the Truth Ring and hold it before the Water Horse's eyes. Its reflection in the polished silver shows the creature's true form — a shadowy, ancient spirit of the deep, its too-many teeth part of a grin that stretches into eternity.

"You carry the ring of truth," it hisses, its voice now a chorus of drowning whispers. "Very well, mortal. You have seen me for what I am. I will not drag you to the depths — that pleasure belongs only to the deceived."

The kelpie rears back and vanishes into the sea with a splash that soaks your crew. When the spray clears, a single iridescent scale floats on the water — a token of your victory.

You take the scale. It pulses with a warm, gentle light.

(+3 points. The Water Horse has been outsmarted.)

island_fiery_pigs.name: Island of the Fiery Pigs
island_fiery_pigs.description: An island covered in blackened grass. Pigs made of living flame trot across the scorched earth.
island_fiery_pigs.detailed_desc:
The grass on this island is charred black. Small fires smolder everywhere. And trotting across the landscape are PIGS — but pigs made entirely of flame, their bodies crackling with fire, their eyes burning coals.

Wherever they walk, the grass ignites. They seem to be... grazing on the ashes? One of them roots in the sooty earth and pulls out a glowing ember, which it eats with evident pleasure.

At the center of the island, a stone altar stands untouched by fire. An inscription reads:

'To calm the Fiery Pigs, you must give them what they crave — '
'not water, not earth, but the memory of what was lost.'
'A sacrifice of ash for ash, of fire for fire.'

The pigs snort, and small fireballs shoot from their nostrils. They look hungry. Not for food — for something else.

blocked.southwest: the fiery pigs surge around you — the heat is unbearable

island_revolving_castle.name: Island of the Revolving Castle
island_revolving_castle.description: A castle made of black stone that slowly rotates on a central axis. Its doors spin past at regular intervals.
island_revolving_castle.detailed_desc:
A strange castle dominates this island — a fortress of black obsidian that turns slowly, ceaselessly, like a great stone top. It has been turning for so long that the ground around it is worn into a perfect circle.

It has four doors — each one a different color: Red, Blue, Green, and Black. As the castle revolves, each door passes a stone platform at the base, staying aligned for only a few heartbeats before continuing its rotation.

The doors are locked. The keyhole on the Red Door turns restlessly, as if waiting for a matching key...

A stone plaque reads: 'Enter at the turning of the world. The right door at the right time. Choose poorly, and the castle will never let you go.'

The castle GRINDS as it turns. It sounds almost alive. Like a great stone beast, breathing in slow circles.

You could try to USE the REVOLVING KEY on the DOOR, or EXAMINE the WALLS for a secret entrance, or WAIT for the right moment.

blocked.enter: the castle is still revolving — the doors spin past too quickly to enter
blocked.in: the castle is still revolving — the doors spin past too quickly to enter

castle_entrance.name: The Castle Entrance
castle_entrance.description: A dark hallway of polished obsidian, lit by a faint red glow from a door at the far end.
castle_entrance.detailed_desc:
You step through the entrance into a dark hallway. The walls are polished black obsidian, smooth as glass. A faint red glow emanates from a door at the far end — the Red Door, now open.

The air is still and cold. The grinding of the castle has stopped, and the silence is profound.

Carved into the wall beside you, an inscription reads:

'The heart of the castle beats in the Red Chamber. Enter, and claim what was left for you.'

The Red Door beckons.

castle_red.name: The Red Door — Heart of the Castle
castle_red.description: A circular chamber of black obsidian. A single shaft of red light illuminates a stone pedestal at the center.
castle_red.detailed_desc:
The Red Door swings open with a groan of ancient hinges. You step into a circular chamber of polished black obsidian. The walls curve inward overhead, forming a dome. A single shaft of red light — from where, you cannot tell — illuminates a STONE PEDESTAL at the exact center of the room.

On the pedestal rests a SILVER NET, finely woven, shimmering like moonlight on water.

The castle shudders around you, as if acknowledging your presence. You have entered the heart of the turning world.

castle_blue.name: The Blue Door — Chamber of Storms
castle_blue.description: A room filled with howling wind and freezing rain. The floor is slick with ice.
castle_blue.detailed_desc:
The Blue Door opens onto a tempest. Wind howls through the chamber, whipping rain into your face. The floor is treacherous with black ice.

In the center of the storm, barely visible through the sleet, a pedestal holds a single item: a pair of WAX EARPLUGS.

The storm is too fierce. You cannot reach it without being frozen solid. This door was not meant for you.

castle_green.name: The Green Door — Garden of Stone
castle_green.description: A room that was once a garden. Petrified vines hang from the ceiling like frozen snakes.
castle_green.detailed_desc:
The Green Door opens onto what was once a lush garden. Everything — vines, flowers, a small fountain — has turned to grey stone. The air is dry and still.

In the center of the garden, a stone table holds a SCROLL etched in stone, but the text is too weathered to read. Whatever wisdom was here has been lost to time.

This door, too, was sealed long ago. The Green path holds nothing for you now.

castle_black.name: The Black Door — The Void
castle_black.description: Absolute darkness. The floor may or may not exist. You cannot tell.
castle_black.detailed_desc:
You open the Black Door and step into — nothing.

There is no light. No sound. No sensation of floor beneath your feet, yet you do not fall. You simply... exist, in a space that has no dimensions.

A voice — perhaps your own thoughts — whispers: 'You were not meant to enter here. The Black Door is the end of all journeys, not the middle. Go back.'

You step backward and find yourself outside again, shaken.

island_trumpet.name: Island of the Giant Trumpet
island_trumpet.description: A barren island with a single giant brass trumpet mounted on a cliff, pointing out to sea.
island_trumpet.detailed_desc:
This island is a bare rock with a single feature: an enormous BRASS TRUMPET, as large as a ship, mounted on a stone pedestal at the edge of a cliff.

The trumpet points out to sea. A mechanism of gears and levers connects to a set of giant leather bellows behind it. One pull of the lever would produce a sound that would carry for miles.

A chilling inscription is carved into the pedestal:

'One blast of this trumpet will shatter any ship within a league. The sound is the voice of the sea god's anger. Do not sound it unless you wish to drown all who hear.'

But you notice something: there is a small CLOTH stuffed into the trumpet's bell. Someone else was here before you, and they tried to muffle it.

There are also WAX EARPLUGS lying nearby. Whoever was here left in a hurry.

WARNING: The trumpet's bellows are filling again. If you try to leave without muffling the trumpet, the blast will deafen your crew!

blocked.northwest: THE TRUMPET BLASTS as you try to leave! The sound is deafening! You stagger back, ears ringing. You need to muffle the trumpet first, or protect yourself with earplugs!

island_demons.name: Island of the Demon Smith
island_demons.description: An island wreathed in black smoke. The ground is hot to the touch. A forge burns with flames that are blacker than night.
island_demons.detailed_desc:
The air is thick with smoke and the smell of brimstone. The ground is black glass — melted and cooled volcanic rock that crunches under your feet. Each step sounds like breaking bones.

At the center of the island, a massive FORGE burns with BLACK FLAMES — fire that is darker than the smoke around it, fire that drinks light instead of giving it.

A DEMON works the forge — a figure of cracked stone and living ember, his eyes like cooling coals. He hammers a piece of black iron into a coin.

CLANG. Each strike sends out a wave of heat that warps the air. CLANG. Each coin bears the face of a different screaming soul.

The demon looks up. 'Ah. A customer. Come to trade? I don't get many visitors. Most people see the black flames and turn back. Cowards.' He grins. His teeth are made of molten gold.

Coins of black iron are piled on a table nearby.

island_golden_pillar.name: Island of the Golden Pillar
island_golden_pillar.description: A pillar of solid gold rises from the sea, impossibly tall. A silver fishnet hangs from its apex.
island_golden_pillar.detailed_desc:
A PILLAR of solid gold rises from the sea — so tall that its top disappears into the clouds. It is wider than a house, and polished to a mirror shine. You can see your reflection in it — and behind your reflection, the reflection of your crew, and behind them, the reflection of the entire sea.

Carved into its surface are images of fish, ships, and sea creatures — the history of the Atlantic, written in gold. You see ships from every era: curraghs, Viking longships, Spanish galleons, modern trawlers.

Near the top — just visible at the cloud line — a SILVER NET hangs from a hook. Something gleams inside it. Something golden.

At the base of the pillar, a tidepool contains a single, perfectly round opening — a keyhole. Or a socket. Or a mouth.

An inscription at the base reads:

'He who would climb to heaven's gate must first see what the silver net makes great. The golden pillar holds the sky. The silver net holds the answer. Catch what glitters, but know its weight.'

The pillar hums faintly, like a tuning fork struck by the gods.

homecoming_beach.name: The Coast of Ireland — Home at Last
homecoming_beach.description: The familiar grey strand where your father fell. The tide murmurs like an old storyteller.
homecoming_beach.detailed_desc:
After countless islands and wonders — after giant ants and talking cats, after laughing kings and weeping monks, after glass bridges and silver bells — your curragh finally scrapes onto a familiar shore.

This is the strand where your father was murdered. You recognise the black rocks, the twisted tree that has grown a little more twisted in your absence, the exact spot where Ailill Ochair Ága drew his last breath.

The tide is coming in. It sounds different now — less like water, more like time. Three years of voyaging, and you have returned to the same patch of sand.

Your crew steps onto the beach behind you. Diurán's hand is on his sword — he's a poet, not a fighter, but he'll fight. Conganchnes stands at your shoulder, his unbreakable skin gleaming. Fergus hangs back, watching the sky for omens.

And there — by a driftwood fire — sits someone you recognise.

The DRUID from your village. The same old man who gave you the Magic Thread and told you to take three times nine men. He is stirring a small pot, the same pot he was stirring three years ago, as if no time has passed at all.

homecoming_hill.name: The Hill of Ailill Ochair Ága
homecoming_hill.description: A windswept hill overlooking the Aran Islands. A cairn of grey stones marks where the Wolf fell.
homecoming_hill.detailed_desc:
You climb the hill above the strand, following the path your father walked a thousand times before. The wind is stronger up here — it whips your hair and tugs at your cloak.

At the summit stands a CAIRN of grey stones, each one stacked with care. This is where your father's body was laid to rest. The stones are weathered now — three years of Atlantic wind and rain have softened their edges, but the cairn stands firm.

From here you can see the whole island: the stone huts of your village, the grey thread of the road, the endless sea that carried you to the edge of the world and brought you back.

A small offering lies at the base of the cairn: a few wildflowers, a crust of bread, a half-full cup of mead. Someone still remembers.

homecoming_choice.name: The Point of Decision
homecoming_choice.description: A rocky promontory overlooking the sea. This is where it ends.
homecoming_choice.detailed_desc:
You walk the narrow path to the edge of the cliff. The sea crashes below, the same sea that carried you to thirty islands and thirty wonders.

Ahead, the sun is setting over the Atlantic — gold and crimson bleeding into the water like a wound, like a blessing, like the end of a story.

mill_exterior.name: The Mill of the Sea — Exterior
mill_exterior.description: A towering mill of black stone stands on a cliff, its great wheel dipping into the sea and churning the water into foam.
mill_exterior.detailed_desc:
A massive MILL of black stone dominates this island. It stands on a cliff at the edge of the sea, and its great wheel — as wide as your entire curragh — dips into the water, churning the sea into white foam. The grinding noise is immense — a deep, rhythmic GRIND-GRIND-GRIND that you feel in your teeth.

The sea around the island is violent — whirlpools form and dissolve where the wheel churns. The water looks milk-white from the constant grinding.

An old man shuffles near the entrance to the mill, muttering to himself. He does not seem to have noticed you yet.

A stone archway leads INTO the mill proper. The grinding is louder from inside.

mill_interior.name: The Mill of the Sea — Grinding Chamber
mill_interior.description: Inside the mill. Great bronze gears the size of houses turn slowly, meshing with crushing force. The floor vibrates.
mill_interior.detailed_desc:
You step inside the mill, and the noise doubles. Great GEARS of bronze and iron turn in the dim light — each one the size of a house, meshing with a force that could crush stone to powder.

In the center of the chamber, a massive MILLSTONE — a wheel of black granite taller than three men — grinds against a stone base. Between them, seawater pours in and emerges as... nothing. It simply disappears, ground into the fabric of reality.

A fragment of the millstone lies on the floor — broken off, perhaps by a previous visitor who tried and failed to stop the mill. It is HEAVY.

The gears turn with terrible purpose. If you could jam something into them — something heavy and strong — you might stop the wheel. The old guardian said you can only 'feed' the mill. Perhaps that is the answer: give it something heavy enough to choke on.

island_sheep.name: Island of Black & White Sheep
island_sheep.description: An island split down the middle — a field of black grass on one side, white grass on the other. Sheep cross between them and change color as they walk.
island_sheep.detailed_desc:
This island is divided into two perfect halves.

To the left, a field of BLACK grass, so dark it seems to drink the light. White sheep graze there, but as you watch, one crosses the invisible boundary — and the moment it steps onto the black grass, its fleece turns BLACK. It continues grazing, apparently unconcerned by its transformation.

To the right, a field of WHITE grass, so pale it glows faintly. Black sheep graze there, turning white the moment they cross over.

A narrow path runs between the two fields, bordered by neither black nor white grass — a grey ribbon of packed earth. At the far end stands a figure in a tattered cloak, watching you.

Across both fields, a GHOSTLY SHEPHERD walks slowly, his crook trailing through the grass. He leaves no footprints.

blocked.northeast: The sheep have blocked the path! A wall of black and white wool surges across the trail. The shepherd's riddle echoes in your mind: 'Neither black nor white, yet containing both.'

sheep_pasture.name: The Shepherd's Pasture
sheep_pasture.description: A quiet pasture at the far end of the grey path, where a single fleece hangs on a wooden post.
sheep_pasture.detailed_desc:
The grey path opens into a small, peaceful pasture. The shepherd's crook stands planted in the ground, and hanging from it is a FLEECE — shimmering, shifting between black and white as you look at it.

The ghostly shepherd sits on a grey stone, watching you with twilight eyes.

'You answered the riddle,' he says softly. 'The fleece is yours. It is neither black nor white — it is both. It is the space between. Wear it well, traveler, and remember: the truest path is never one thing or the other, but the grey road between extremes.'

The sheep have parted to let you pass. The way back to the sea is clear.

island_horses.name: Island of Giant Horses
island_horses.description: A wide, grassy island where horses the size of war elephants gallop across the plains, their hooves shaking the earth.
island_horses.detailed_desc:
This is an island of grass and thunder.

HERDS of GIANT HORSES gallop across the plains — each one the size of a small house, their manes streaming like banners, their hooves striking the earth with the force of falling trees. The ground trembles constantly.

At the center of the herd stands the STALLION KING — a magnificent white horse larger than all the others, his mane flowing like sea-foam, his eyes burning with wild intelligence. He watches you with the unmistakable expression of a king who does not suffer fools.

The herd mills around him, snorting and stamping. They do not attack — yet. But they make it clear: you are not welcome here unless you prove yourself.

blocked.southeast: The herd encircles you! The Stallion King snorts a warning. You must calm the horses or fight them before you can leave.

island_flaming_cat.name: Island of the Flaming Cat
island_flaming_cat.description: A small, warm island dominated by a single pedestal of black stone. A golden crystal rests atop it, pulsing with inner light.
island_flaming_cat.detailed_desc:
This island is small — barely more than a large rock jutting from the sea. But it is unnaturally warm, as if heated from below. The air shimmers with heat haze.

At the center stands a PEDESTAL of black obsidian, carved with images of cats in various stages of growth — from tiny kittens to enormous, flame-wreathed beasts.

On top of the pedestal rests a SUNSTONE — a golden crystal that pulses with captured sunlight, casting warm, dancing beams across the island.

A LITTLE CAT sits at the base of the pedestal — a tiny, rust-colored kitten with emerald eyes. It purrs and rubs against the stone, gazing up at the crystal with obvious adoration.

When you approach, it looks up at you and mews. It seems to be saying: 'This is mine. But maybe — just maybe — we can come to an arrangement.'

wall_of_water.name: The Wall of Water
wall_of_water.description: A towering wall of water rises before your ship, impossibly high, stretching from the seafloor to the clouds.
wall_of_water.detailed_desc:
A WALL OF WATER rises before you — a vertical ocean, stretching from the depths below to the heavens above. It is translucent, greenish, moving with a slow, powerful current that defies all nature.

The wall hums — a deep, resonant sound like a mountain singing. Your curragh rocks in the turbulence at its base. Spray drenches you.

Fergus stares, his face pale. 'Captain... I have never seen anything like this. It is a boundary. The sea itself has become a wall. We cannot sail through — it would crush us. But we cannot sail around it either. It stretches as far as I can see.'

There must be a way to calm the waters. The Magic Thread on your mast... the Silver Bell... something that can speak to the sea's anger.

blocked.northwest: The wall of water thunders before you. You cannot leave until you find a way through.
blocked.through: A towering wall of water blocks your path. You must calm the waters before you can pass through.

island_oxen.name: Island of the Sacred Oxen
island_oxen.description: A green, misty island where two massive white oxen with golden horns stand motionless, watching the sea.
island_oxen.detailed_desc:
A green island, covered in mist that glows with a pale, golden light. The grass is thick and soft — it feels like walking on clouds.

Two SACRED OXEN stand in the center of the island — magnificent white beasts with horns of pure gold. They are as still as statues, their breath forming clouds in the cool air. Their eyes are deep, dark pools — ancient, patient, knowing.

They do not move as you approach. But they WATCH you.

One of them lowers its massive head, presenting its golden horn as if offering it. Or perhaps it is a challenge. The meaning is unclear.

The smaller ox lows softly — a sound like a distant thunder, mournful and beautiful.

oxen_glade.name: The Oxen's Glade
oxen_glade.description: A peaceful glade where the sacred oxen have made their home for centuries. The grass here glows faintly with a golden light.
oxen_glade.detailed_desc:
You step into the sacred glade, and the mist parts around you like a curtain.

The oxen stand at the center, their golden horns casting warm light in all directions. The grass beneath your feet glows faintly, as if infused with gold dust.

The larger ox lowers its head and gently places its golden horn at your feet. It steps back and lows softly — a sound of peace, of offering.

'Take it,' a voice seems to say — not in words, but in understanding. 'Take what you need, and go in peace. We have guarded this island long enough. Perhaps it is time for the horn to see the world beyond the mist.'

The smaller ox nuzzles your hand. Its breath is warm and smells of hay and ancient sunlight.

freshwater_well.name: The Strand of the Freshwater Well
freshwater_well.description: A sandy beach on the edge of a dark sea. A single well of white stone stands at the high-tide mark, shimmering with otherworldly light.
freshwater_well.detailed_desc:
A strand of pale sand curves along the edge of a dark sea. The waves here are gentle — they lap at the shore like a tired animal, making soft, hushing sounds.

At the high-tide mark, a WELL of white stone rises from the sand. It is ancient — the stone is worn smooth by centuries of wind and salt.

Inside the well, WATER shimmers — not reflecting the grey sky above, but glowing with its own silvery light. It is the clearest water you have ever seen, and looking into it, you see not your reflection, but... something else. A path. A door. A truth you have not yet faced.

A small cup of horn hangs from a peg on the well's rim, as if waiting for visitors.

An inscription is carved around the well's rim:

'Drink and see what is hidden. Take and carry the light. But know this: the water shows only truth, and truth is not always kind.'

great_fish_belly.name: The Great Fish — Belly of the Beast
great_fish_belly.description: You are inside the belly of a fish the size of a cathedral. The walls pulse wetly. It is dark, hot, and the air smells of brine and bile.
great_fish_belly.detailed_desc:
Darkness. Warmth. A wet, rhythmic pulse all around you.\
\
You are INSIDE something. Something alive.\
\
The walls are slick and pink, flexing with each slow contraction. The floor — if it can be called a floor — is spongy and uneven, slick with half-digested seawater. The air is thick and warm, and you taste salt and iron on your tongue.\
\
Your curragh is intact — the fish swallowed your boat whole, and now you drift in this fleshy chamber, surrounded by the slow, terrible digestion of the deep.\
\
There are no exits. No doors. No light.\
\
But the walls... they are thin in places. Thin enough to cut through. Thin enough to BURN through. If you have something sharp, or something that burns, you might be able to cut your way out.

great_fish_carcass.name: The Great Fish — Carcass
great_fish_carcass.description: The fish floats lifeless on the surface, a gaping wound in its side. Your boat drifts nearby.
great_fish_carcass.detailed_desc:
The Great Fish floats belly-up on the dark water. It is enormous — the size of a small island. Its scales are the color of storm clouds, and its dead eye stares at nothing.\
\
You clamber out through the wound you made, gasping for clean air. Your crew follows, coughing and cheering.\
\
Fergus kneels on the fish's belly. 'I'm never eating fish again. Never. Not even on Fridays.'\
\
Between the fish's gaping jaws, you spot something gleaming — a single massive tooth, broken off during the swallowing. It is serrated, curved, and as long as your forearm. It could be a weapon. A reminder. Both.\
\
Take the FISH TOOTH before you go.

island_fountain.name: Island of the Fountain
island_fountain.description: A small, green island with a single white stone fountain at its center. The water glows with a pale, milky luminescence.
island_fountain.detailed_desc:
This island is a perfect circle of green grass, no larger than a village green. At its center stands a FOUNTAIN of white stone, ancient and weather-worn, carved with spirals and knotwork that seem to shift when you look at them sideways.\
\
Water flows from the fountain — not clear, but MILK-WHITE, shimmering with an inner light. It pools in a basin below and overflows into a channel that feeds the grass.\
\
An inscription circles the basin, worn but legible:\
\
    'Drink and you shall dream.\
     Take and you shall carry.\
     Give and you shall heal.'\
\
The water smells faintly of honey and fresh cream. It looks drinkable. It looks like it might do something.

island_silence.name: Island of Silenced Music
island_silence.description: A beautiful valley where everything is muted. The birds open their beaks but no sound comes out. The wind blows but does not rustle the leaves.
island_silence.detailed_desc:
This valley should be full of sound — birds singing, wind rustling through the leaves, a stream chattering over stones. But there is NOTHING.\
\
The silence is so complete you can hear your own blood moving through your veins. You can hear your eyelids blinking. The absence of noise is a physical weight.\
\
The valley is beautiful — green grass, flowering trees, a crystal stream — but it is a beauty that has been frozen, mummified, preserved in silence.\
\
At the far end of the valley, on a throne of grey stone, sits a figure draped in flowing grey robes. It does not move. It does not breathe. But you know it is waiting.\
\
An iron bell hangs from a branch of a dead tree nearby. When you look at it, you feel an overwhelming urge to ring it — but also a deep, primal fear of what might happen if you do.\
\
The silence here is not natural. It is enforced. By something. Or someone.

silence_grove.name: The Silent Grove
silence_grove.description: A small grove of silver-leaved trees surrounding a white clearing. The Silent Bell hangs on a branch, utterly still.
silence_grove.detailed_desc:
Beyond the valley, hidden behind a curtain of silver-leaved willows, you find a small clearing. The grass here is soft and white, like moonlit snow.\
\
At the center of the clearing, a single dead tree stands. Hanging from its lowest branch is an iron BELL — cold, black, and silent. It does not move, even though there is no wind.\
\
The grey figure does not follow you here. For now, you are alone with the bell.\
\
You can TAKE the Silent Bell. It makes no sound when you touch it.

promised_land.name: The Promised Land
promised_land.description: A land of impossible beauty — golden fruit hangs from silver trees, rivers of wine flow through meadows of eternal spring, and the air smells of home.
promised_land.detailed_desc:
This is the island at the end of the world.\
\
It is everything you have ever wanted. The sky is the perfect blue of a summer afternoon that never fades. The trees bear fruit of pure gold and silver. Rivers of wine and honey wind through meadows of flowers that bloom in colours you have never seen.\
\
The air is warm and gentle. The grass is soft as silk. In the distance, you can see white buildings of marble and crystal — a city that gleams like a promise.\
\
Your crew stands frozen, tears streaming down their faces. Diurán whispers: 'This is it, Captain. This is what the poets sing about. This is the Land of Promise.'\
\
A figure approaches — a luminous being in white robes, its face radiating infinite kindness and peace.\
\
It opens its arms and speaks:\
\
'Welcome, Mael Duin. Welcome home. You have crossed the edges of the world, braved monsters and wonders, and now you stand at the threshold of the Land of Promise. Here there is no pain, no sorrow, no death. Stay with us forever. All you have to do is say yes.'\
\
The offer hangs in the air. It is the most tempting thing you have ever heard.\
\
But somewhere — far away, across the sea — there is a small grey island where a woman waits. And a child who grew up without a father. And a story that is not yet finished.

island_giant.name: Island of the Giant Killer
island_giant.description: A rocky island dominated by a high cliff. A monstrous giant perches on top, silhouetted against the grey sky, a pile of stones beside him.
island_giant.detailed_desc:
This island is little more than a jagged rock jutting from the sea — a single, steep-sided CLIFF that rises a hundred feet above the waves. The rock is dark basalt, streaked with white where seabirds have nested for centuries.

At the top of the cliff, silhouetted against the grey sky, stands the GIANT. He is massive — twenty feet of crude muscle and malice — and beside him lies a pile of stones, each one large enough to crush a man. His shadow falls across the water like a stain.

The only way to approach is by sea, and the giant has already seen you. His arm draws back. A stone is coming.

The shore is rocky but passable. A narrow path leads to the base of the cliff.

treasure_cave.name: Island of the Treasure
treasure_cave.description: A small, barren island with a single dark cave at its center. The mouth is blocked by a massive serpent coiled in the shadows.
treasure_cave.detailed_desc:
A small, barren island of grey stone and sparse grass. Nothing grows here — the soil is too thin, the wind too harsh.

At the center of the island, a CAVE mouth yawns in the rock. It is dark inside, but you can see a faint golden glow emanating from the depths — the glint of ancient treasure.

Coiled before the cave entrance is a massive SERPENT, its scales shimmering with a deep, oily green. It is the size of a small ship, and its body completely blocks the way in. Its eyes — vertical slits of gold — open and fix on you with ancient hunger.

It hisses, tasting the air. It knows what you want. It knows you will have to go through it.

blocked.in: The serpent blocks the cave entrance with its massive body. You must deal with it first — FIGHT it, GIVE it the Antidote Herb, or BRIBE it with treasure.
blocked.enter: The serpent blocks the cave entrance with its massive body. You must deal with it first.

island_dog.name: Island of the Dog
island_dog.description: A grassy mound rises from the sea. At its summit, a stone pedestal holds a gleaming silver torc. A massive hound lies beside it, ever watchful.
island_dog.detailed_desc:
A gentle, grassy island — a single green mound rising from the grey sea like the back of a sleeping whale. The grass is soft and thick, and wildflowers grow in scattered patches.

At the summit of the mound stands a stone PEDESTAL, ancient and weathered. Upon it rests a SILVER TORC — a beautiful neck-ring of woven silver wire, gleaming with the light of a thousand years. It is clearly a masterwork of ancient craftsmanship.

Before the pedestal, curled like a guard who has never abandoned his post, lies a GREAT HOUND the size of a small horse. Its coat is iron-grey, and its eyes glow like banked embers. It watches you approach with the patient stillness of a creature that has waited centuries.

It does not attack. Not yet. But it makes it clear: the torc is not yours to take lightly.

island_lion.name: Island of the Lion
island_lion.description: A scrub-covered island with a large cave at its center. A mountain lion crouches before it, wounded and furious.
island_lion.detailed_desc:
A harsh island of scrub brush and sharp rocks. The wind whistles through the thorny bushes, creating an eerie, keening sound.

At the center of the island, a wide CAVE mouth opens into the hillside. Before it, crouched in a posture of pure aggression, is a MOUNTAIN LION. Its coat is the colour of dried grass, and its muscles ripple beneath the skin with coiled power.

But you notice something — a deep GASH along its flank, weeping and infected. The beast is in agony, and its fury is born of pain. Its roars are as much anguish as anger.

You could FIGHT it (with Magic Harpoon or Giant's Club), USE the Silver Bell to calm it, or TALK to it with the Speaking Feather to learn of its wound.

anchorite_cave.name: The Anchorite's Cave
anchorite_cave.description: A small cave on a lonely rock, just large enough for one man to shelter. A single candle burns within, casting a warm, steady light.
anchorite_cave.detailed_desc:
A solitary rock rises from the sea — barely large enough to be called an island. On it, a small CAVE has been worn into the stone by wind and wave. Inside, a single CANDLE burns with a flame that does not flicker, though the wind howls outside.

Sitting cross-legged at the mouth of the cave is a man in a simple grey robe. His face is weathered by decades of salt spray and contemplation. His eyes are calm — the calm of someone who has stopped running. Beside him, a small wooden cross rests on a stone.

He looks up as you approach, and smiles — a warm, genuine smile that makes the grey day feel brighter. The sea around the rock is unusually calm, as if the water itself respects his peace.

There is nothing to take here. No treasure. No puzzle. Only a man who has been waiting to speak with you.
